'''Fernando Ruiz Hierro''' ({{IPA|es|feɾˈnando ˈʝero}}; born 23 March 1968) is a Spanish [[Association football|football]] executive and former player who played as a [[centre-back]], [[sweeper (association football)|sweeper]] or [[defensive midfielder]].

He won five [[La Liga]] and three [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] trophies with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 14 years after signing from [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]], during which he appeared in 601 official matches.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/20120123/54245275481/real-madrid-casillas-hierro-gento.html|title=Casillas, a un paso de Hierro y Gento|trans-title=Casillas, closing in on Hierro and Gento|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|language=es|date=23 January 2012|access-date=30 June 2022}}</ref> He also competed professionally in Qatar and England.

Hierro represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on 89 occasions, appearing in four [[FIFA World Cup|World Cups]] and two [[UEFA European Championship|European Championships]]. He started working as a manager in 2016 with [[Real Oviedo|Oviedo]], being appointed at the helm of the national team two years later.

==Club career==
===Early years and Real Madrid===
Hierro was born in [[Vélez-Málaga]], [[Province of Málaga]]. After beginning his football career at local club [[Vélez CF|Vélez]], he had a very brief youth spell with neighbouring [[CD Málaga]], where he was told he was not good enough for the sport, which prompted a return home.<ref name=RMF>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadridfans.org/hierro.htm|title=Fernando Hierro|publisher=Real Madrid Fans|language=es|year=2012|access-date=27 April 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130415190623/http://www.realmadridfans.org/hierro.htm|archive-date=15 April 2013}}</ref> He eventually made his [[La Liga]] debut with [[Real Valladolid]], being bought by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the summer of 1989 after two solid seasons; youth graduate [[José Luis Caminero]] moved in the opposite direction as part of the deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2020/07/04/5eff185946163f10af8b4596.html|title=Cantera y Real Madrid: El equipazo que se fue de casa|trans-title=Youth system and Real Madrid: The wonder team that left home|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|last=Hurtado|first=José Luis|language=es|date=4 July 2020|access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref>

At Real, Hierro scored seven goals in 37 games in his [[1989–90 La Liga|first season]], and eventually had his position on the field advanced by coach [[Radomir Antić]], continuing his good performances with the addition of goals – he totalled an astonishing 44 league goals in three seasons, 21 alone in [[1991–92 La Liga|1991–92]], a career-best.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD01/HEM/1992/03/09/MD19920309-055.pdf|title=Un gol para un doble liderato|trans-title=One goal for a double first place|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=9 March 1992|access-date=20 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nacion.com/puro-deporte/hierro-recibio-el-carino-y-reconocimiento-de-todo-el-madridismo/Z5FUQ5YNYJDDZJTSQKAA4VVFI4/story/|title=Hierro recibió el cariño y reconocimiento de todo el madridismo|trans-title=Hierro received the love and acknowledgement of the entire ''madridismo''|newspaper=La Nación|language=es|date=21 May 2005|access-date=18 May 2018}}</ref> For years, he often partnered [[Manolo Sanchís]] in the centre of defence, being instrumental in the conquest of five leagues and three [[UEFA Champions League]] trophies<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0155-0e6a20959a54-7745f9013b98-1000--1997-98-seventh-heaven-for-madrid/|title=1997/98: Seventh heaven for Madrid|publisher=UEFA|date=20 May 1998|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01ff-0e7e669a87d0-6b476738d04f-1000--1999-2000-real-madrid-cf-3-0-valencia-cf-report/|title=1999/2000 Real Madrid CF 3–0 Valencia CF: Report|publisher=UEFA|date=14 July 2012|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0185-0e6a414977dc-840dff896fae-1000--madrid-win-ninth-european-crown/|title=Madrid win ninth European crown|publisher=UEFA|date=15 May 2002|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref> and being named [[Captain (association football)|captain]] after the latter's retirement.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/futbol/2022-06-15/real-madrid-marcelo-capitan-despedida-raul-florentino-ramos-casillas-hierro-sanchis_3441826/|title=Marcelo, por fin un capitán del Real Madrid se va sin que Florentino le considere una estafa|trans-title=Marcelo, finally a Real Madrid captain leaves without Florentino thinking of him as a fraud|newspaper=[[El Confidencial]]|last=Marín|first=Kike|language=es|date=15 June 2022|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref>

On 24 March 2002, Hierro scored a [[hat-trick]] in a 3–1 home win against [[Real Zaragoza]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=20205.html|title=Spain round-up: Hierro hits hat-trick in Madrid victory|publisher=UEFA|date=24 March 2002|access-date=26 May 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110602080017/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=20205.html|archive-date=2 June 2011}}</ref> although the [[2001–02 La Liga|ultimate champions]] would be [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]. He was released at the end of the [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03 season]] alongside manager [[Vicente del Bosque]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0252-0cdbd82bba6d-2cfe5b5ce040-1000--axe-falls-on-del-bosque-and-hierro/|title=Axe falls on Del Bosque and Hierro|publisher=UEFA|date=24 June 2003|access-date=26 May 2010}}</ref> under rather unceremonious circumstances; having appeared in 497 top-division matches over the course of 16 seasons (105 goals), he then chose a lucrative move to the wealthy but developing [[Middle East]] football industry, joining [[Qatar]]'s [[Al-Rayyan SC|Al-Rayyan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0194-0f84500776ff-c4b94acb7e9c-1000--hierro-embraces-qatar-challenge/|title=Hierro embraces Qatar challenge|publisher=UEFA|date=27 August 2003|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref>

===Bolton Wanderers===
After just one year, Hierro returned to Europe to sign with [[Premier League]] side [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/0257-0de6721495ac-213c4fc1adc1-1000--bolton-ready-for-hierro-worship/|title=Bolton ready for Hierro worship|publisher=UEFA|last=Eeles|first=Alex|date=12 August 2004|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref> on the advice of his English teammate at Real Madrid [[Steve McManaman]], and teaming up with another former player of that club, [[Iván Campo]]. He scored once during his tenure, which came in a 3–2 loss at [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] in December 2004<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/4072043.stm|title=Norwich 3–2 Bolton|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=11 December 2004|access-date=1 September 2009}}</ref> and, even though hard-pressed by fans and manager [[Sam Allardyce]] to stay for a further campaign,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=775846.html|title=Hierro wise to the benefits of English approach|publisher=UEFA|last=Hunter|first=Graham|date=18 November 2008|access-date=15 June 2018}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> he announced his retirement from professional football on 10 May 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/0252-0cddb9b6afc0-ce27cb194148-1000--hero-hierro-calls-it-a-day/|title=Hero Hierro calls it a day|publisher=UEFA|last=Hall|first=Andy|date=10 May 2005|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
Hierro was [[Cap (sport)|capped]] 89 times for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] and scored 29 goals, being only surpassed by [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] (who also took over his captain armband in June 2002 when he retired), [[Álvaro Morata]], [[David Silva]], [[Fernando Torres]] and [[David Villa]]. He made his debut on 20 September 1989 – freshly signed by Madrid – in a 1–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] victory over [[Poland national football team|Poland]] in [[A Coruña]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.abc.es/nav/Navigate.exe/hemeroteca/madrid/abc/1989/09/21/081.html|title=1–0: El pie de Míchel marcó ante Polonia el camino que España buscará en Hungria|trans-title=1–0: Míchel's foot set track in Poland that Spain will seek in Hungary|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|page=81|language=es|date=21 September 1989|access-date=13 July 2016}}</ref> and appeared for the nation in the [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]] (although only as a squad member), [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]], [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]] and [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002]] [[FIFA World Cup]]s, as well as [[UEFA Euro 1996]] (where he missed a penalty as Spain crashed out to hosts [[England national football team|England]] in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|shootout]]) and [[UEFA Euro 2000|2000]].<ref name=RSSSF>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/hierro-intlg.html|title=Fernando Ruiz Hierro – Goals in International Matches|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|last=Pierrend|first=Jose Luís|date=15 February 2003|access-date=12 September 2006}}</ref>

One of Hierro's most important goals came during the [[1994 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|1994 World Cup qualification]], as he headed the winner against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] that allowed ten-men Spain to qualify for the final tournament in the United States.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/gradario/hemeroteca/2015/11/16/santiago-canizares-debutaba-seleccion-siendo-celtico/00031447706329009178366.htm|title=Cañizares debutaba en la selección siendo céltico|trans-title=Cañizares made national team debut as a ''céltico''|newspaper=[[La Voz de Galicia]]|last=Fernández|first=Alberto|language=es|date=17 November 2015|access-date=28 June 2016}}</ref> In the finals, he scored after an individual effort against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] in the [[Single-elimination tournament|round of 16]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://global.espn.com/football/story/1023075/espnsoccernet-la-liga-quiniela-week-21-il-grande-spagna?src=com|title=Week 21 – Il grande stratega|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|last=Álvarez|first=Eduardo|date=10 February 2012|access-date=14 June 2018}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> before his team was eliminated by [[Italy national football team|Italy]] in the quarter-finals following a 2–1 loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/1994/luglio/10/resurrezione_dell_Arrigo_co_0_9407103435.shtml|title=La resurrezione dell'Arrigo|trans-title=The resurrection of the Arrigo|newspaper=[[Corriere della Sera]]|language=it|date=10 July 1994|access-date=7 January 2015}}</ref>

==Coaching and executive career==
Although he had already been in charge for a few weeks, Hierro was officially presented as [[sporting director]] of the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] in late September 2007.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2007/09/24/futbol/1190642518.html|title=Hierro será presentado el jueves como director deportivo de la Federación|trans-title=Hierro to be presented Thursday as sporting director of the Federation|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=es|date=24 September 2007|access-date=27 April 2009}}</ref> He remained four years in the position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/01ec-0e76c1ebeafb-495466447698-1000--triumphant-spain-share-lesson-in-humility/|title=Triumphant Spain share lesson in humility|publisher=UEFA|last=Roxburgh|first=Andy|author-link=Andy Roxburgh|date=31 December 2010|access-date=14 June 2018}}</ref>

Hierro returned to his native region in July 2011, being appointed [[Málaga CF]]'s [[director of football]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ideal.es/granada/20110707/deportes/mas-futbol/malaga-fernando-hierro-ultima-estrella-jeque-201107071316.html|title=Málaga CF: Fernando Hierro, la última estrella del jeque|trans-title=Málaga CF: Fernando Hierro, the sheikh's latest star|newspaper=[[Ideal (newspaper)|Ideal]]|last=Badía|first=Ana M.|language=es|date=7 July 2011|access-date=22 March 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/es/news/27/liga-de-espa%C3%B1a/2011/11/24/2772315/m%C3%A1laga-hierro-anuncia-que-no-es-prioridad-fichar-en-enero|title=Málaga: Hierro anuncia que no es prioridad fichar en enero|trans-title=Málaga: Hierro announces there are no urgencies to sign in January|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|language=es|date=24 November 2011|access-date=22 March 2012}}</ref> On 28 May 2012, even though the club [[2011–12 La Liga|finished fourth]] and [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|qualified for the Champions League]] for the first time ever, he left his position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1640871.html|title=Hierro quits as Malaga general manager|publisher=FIFA|date=28 May 2012|access-date=30 July 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120601143358/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1640871.html|archive-date=1 June 2012}}</ref>

[[File:ESP-RUS (21).jpg|thumb|Hierro at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]]]]
On 10 July 2014, Hierro was named assistant coach of Real Madrid, replacing [[Zinedine Zidane]] – who left to take the reins of [[Real Madrid Castilla]] – in [[Carlo Ancelotti]]'s staff.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2014/07/10/portada/1405015257_544900.html|title=Fernando Hierro será el nuevo ayudante de Carlo Ancelotti|trans-title=Fernando Hierro will be Carlo Ancelotti's new assistant|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|last=Colino|first=Carmen|language=es|date=10 July 2014|access-date=18 May 2015}}</ref> He was given his first full managerial role two years later, being appointed at [[Segunda División]] side [[Real Oviedo]] for the [[2016–17 Segunda División|upcoming season]] with the option of a further year;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11827/10307486/fernando-hierro-named-new-boss-of-spanish-side-real-oviedo|title=Fernando Hierro named new boss of Spanish side Real Oviedo|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|last=Kabelu|first=Beya|date=8 June 2016|access-date=8 June 2016}}</ref> on 14 June 2017, after missing out on the [[2017 Segunda División play-offs|promotion playoffs]] on the final matchday, he left the [[Estadio Carlos Tartiere]] by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-espana.net/64569/hierro-departs-real-oviedo|title=Hierro departs Real Oviedo|publisher=Football España|last=Millar|first=Colin|date=14 June 2017|access-date=14 June 2017}}</ref>

Hierro returned to the Spanish Federation as sporting director on 27 November 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/spain/story/3281721/fernando-hierro-reappointed-spanish-football-association-sporting-director|title=Fernando Hierro reappointed Spanish Football Association sporting director|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=27 November 2017|access-date=13 June 2018}}</ref> He was appointed as the manager of Spain on 13 June 2018<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-fernando-hierro-assume-role-head-coach-russia-world-cup|title=OFFICIAL {{!}} Fernando Hierro to assume role as head coach for the Russia World Cup|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|last=Rubio|first=Carmelo|date=13 June 2018|access-date=14 June 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615023600/http://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-fernando-hierro-assume-role-head-coach-russia-world-cup|archive-date=15 June 2018}}</ref> after the sacking of [[Julen Lopetegui]] two days before their first match at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]], following the latter's decision to join Real Madrid after the tournament.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/13/julen-lopetegui-sacked-spain-manager-real-madrid-job|title=Julen Lopetegui sacked as Spain manager after accepting Real Madrid job|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|last=Lowe|first=Sid|author-link=Sid Lowe|date=13 June 2018|access-date=13 June 2018}}</ref> Two days later, he led the team to a 3–3 [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group B|group stage]] draw against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]];<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/06/15/portugal-vs-spain-world-cup-2018-live-score-latest-updates/|title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores sensational hat-trick as Portugal hold Spain in instant World Cup classic|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=15 June 2018|access-date=15 June 2018}}</ref> on 8 July, following a penalty shootout loss to hosts [[Russia national football team|Russia]] in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Spain vs Russia|round of 16]], he stepped down from his post and also announced that he would not return to his role as sporting director.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-fernando-hierro-steps-down-spain-sporting-director|title=OFFICIAL {{!}} Fernando Hierro steps down as Spain sporting director|publisher=Royal Spanish Football Federation|date=8 July 2018|access-date=8 July 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180708162638/http://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-fernando-hierro-steps-down-spain-sporting-director|archive-date=8 July 2018}}</ref>

On 21 October 2022, Hierro was announced as sporting director of [[C.D. Guadalajara|Guadalajara]] in the Mexican [[Liga MX]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tudn.com/futbol/liga-mx/fernando-hierro-presentacion-director-deportivo-chivas-clausura-2023|title=Fernando Hierro es presentado con Chivas: "Es un gigante que tiene que volver a ilusionar"|trans-title=Fernando Hierro is presented at Chivas: "They are a giant that have to make people dream again"|publisher=[[TUDN (United States TV channel)|TUDN]]|last=R. Yu|first=Kevin|language=es|date=21 October 2022|access-date=26 October 2022}}</ref> In June 2024, he joined [[Saudi Pro League]]'s [[Al-Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]] in the same capacity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/fernando-hierro-joins-ronaldos-al-nassr-sporting-director-2024-06-04/|title=Fernando Hierro joins Ronaldo's Al-Nassr as sporting director|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=4 June 2024|access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref>

==Style of play==
As a [[central defender]], [[Defender (association football)#Sweeper (libero)|sweeper]] or [[defensive midfielder]], Hierro utilised defensive play, a large passing range and goalscoring skill,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iffhs.de/?b4a390f03be4ac07cda14b45fdcdc3bfcdc0aec70aef05|title=World Record of the national championships (1888/89 – 2007)|publisher=[[International Federation of Football History & Statistics]]|access-date=18 December 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071017060701/http://iffhs.de/?b4a390f03be4ac07cda14b45fdcdc3bfcdc0aec70aef05|archive-date=17 October 2007}}</ref> which made him one of the world's most sought-after players.<ref name=RMF/> In addition, he was known for his positional sense, strength in the air, tenacity and the effective ability to time his challenges.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/apr/06/sport.championsleague|title=Last action Hierro|newspaper=The Guardian|date=6 April 2003|access-date=15 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1795294-ranking-the-20-most-intimidating-defenders-in-la-liga-history#slide10|title=Ranking the 20 Most Intimidating Defenders in La Liga History|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|last=Marsden|first=Samuel|date=2 October 2013|access-date=15 June 2018}}</ref>

Regarded as a highly competitive and hard-tackling defender, ''[[The Times]]'' placed Hierro at number 43 in their list of the 50 hardest footballers in history in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.empireonline.com/forum/printable.asp?m=1554851|title=Top 50 hardest footballers|publisher=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]|date=13 August 2007|access-date=23 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019002225/http://www.empireonline.com/forum/printable.asp?m=1554851|archive-date=19 October 2015}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hierro's older brothers, [[Antonio Hierro|Antonio]] and [[Manolo Hierro|Manuel]], were also professional footballers and defenders. The latter paired up with Fernando at Valladolid, as the club finished eighth in [[1987–88 La Liga|1987–88]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.laopiniondemalaga.es/todo-deporte/2013/09/17/fallece-padre-fernando-manolo-hierro/617222.html|title=Fallece el padre de Fernando y Manolo Hierro|trans-title=Father of Fernando and Manolo Hierro dies|newspaper=La Opinión de Málaga|last=Extremera|first=Fran|language=es|date=17 September 2013|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://historias-del-realmadrid.blogspot.pt/2012/11/hierr.html|title=La saga de los Hierro|trans-title=The Hierro saga|publisher=Historias del Real Madrid|language=es|date=26 November 2012|access-date=14 July 2015}}</ref>

In 2021, Hierro began dating Croatian television journalist [[Fani Stipković]], having divorced his wife of 28 years Sonia Ruiz.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/buzz/2023/06/07/647ffd1246163f745d8b45d5.html|title=Fernando Hierro (55) y Fani Stipkovic (40) anuncian que van a ser padres: las reacciones del mundo del fútbol|trans-title=Fernando Hierro (55) and Fani Stipkovic (40) announce they are becoming parents: football world reacts|newspaper=Marca|last=Corbella|first=Enrique|language=es|date=7 June 2023|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref> They married in September 2023 in Mexico<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gloria.hr/gl/scena/price/vjencanje-fani-stipkovic-i-fernanda-hierra-donosimo-detalje-intimne-ceremonije-u-meksiku-15378639|title=Vjenčanje Fani Stipković i Fernanda Hierra: Donosimo detalje intimne ceremonije u Meksiku|trans-title=Fani Stipković and Fernando Hierro's wedding: We bring you all the details of the private ceremony in Mexico|publisher=[[Gloria (magazine)|Gloria]]|last=Leljak|first=Damir|language=hr|date=27 September 2023|access-date=27 September 2023}}</ref> and, the following month, welcomed their first child, Nicolás Valentín.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/tikitakas/el-curioso-nombre-de-fernando-hierro-y-fani-stipkovic-para-su-primer-hijo-juntos-n/|title=El curioso nombre de Fernando Hierro y Fani Stipkovic para su primer hijo juntos|trans-title=Fernando Hierro and Fani Stipkovic's funny name for their first son together|newspaper=Diario AS|last=Córdoba|first=Adrián|language=es|date=31 October 2023|access-date=16 December 2023}}</ref>
